cards.text: Paul, the apostle who wrote this letter, is writing to the church of God in Corinth (1 Corinthians 1:1-2). Last time, he said that if what he eats causes his brother to stumble, he'll never eat meat again (1 Corinthians 8:13). Now he comes out swinging with four questions in a row, starting with "Am I not free? Am I not an apostle?"

cards.question: Paul asks the Corinthians, "Am I not free? Am I not an apostle?" Then he asks if he hasn't seen someone. Who?

cards.text: Then Paul points right at the Corinthians and asks, "Are you yourselves not my workmanship in the Lord?" That's four questions in a row with no breath in between, friend, and I need a NAP after two.

cards.question: Paul says even if he isn't an apostle to others, surely he is to the Corinthians, because they are the ___ of his apostleship in the Lord.

cards.text: Then Paul opens his defense, and his very first question is, "Have we no right to food and to drink?" No big speech, friend, just a man asking if he's allowed to EAT.

cards.question: Next Paul asks if he has the right to take something along, like the other apostles, the Lord's brothers and Cephas do. Cephas is Peter (John 1:42). What does Paul ask about taking along?

cards.text: Then Paul brings up Barnabas. The Holy Spirit had said to set apart Barnabas and Saul, Paul's earlier name, for the work He called them to (Acts 13:2, 9).

cards.question: True or false: Paul asks if he and Barnabas are the only apostles who must work for a living.

cards.text: Then Paul asks, "Who serves as a soldier at his own expense?" Picture a soldier reporting for duty, and the guy at the front desk hands him a BILL for his own sword.

cards.question: Paul asks who serves as a soldier at his own expense, who plants a vineyard and doesn't eat its fruit, and who tends a flock and doesn't drink its milk. What's the point of all three questions?

answers.text: A worker shares in what he works for
A worker should never complain at all
Hard work is always its own reward

cards.text: Then Paul says, in so many words, don't just take MY word for it. He goes straight to the Law of Moses.

cards.question: True or false: The Law of Moses says not to muzzle an ox while it is treading out the grain.
Paul asks, "Is it about oxen that God is concerned?" He says it was written for us, because the plowman and the thresher should also expect to share in the ___.

cards.text: Now Paul turns all that farm talk on himself. He planted something in Corinth, and he asks if it's too much to get something back.

cards.question: Paul asks the Corinthians: if he has sown ___ seed among them, is it too much for him to reap a ___ harvest from them?
Paul says if others have a right to the Corinthians' support, he should have it all the more. True or false: Paul says he made full use of that right.
Paul says he put up with anything instead of using his right to the Corinthians' support. Why?

answers.text: So he wouldn't hinder the gospel of Christ
So no one in Corinth would call him greedy
So the Corinthians would owe him even more

cards.text: Paul's still making his case. He reminds them that those who work in the temple eat of its food, and those who serve at the altar share in its offerings.

cards.question: Paul says those who work in the temple eat of its food. He says the Lord has prescribed the same kind of thing for another group. Who?

cards.text: So Paul builds this whole case, the soldier, the vineyard, the ox, the temple, like a lawyer about to win BIG. And then, real quiet, he says, "But I have not used any of these rights."

cards.question: True or false: Paul says he's writing all this so the Corinthians will start doing something for him.

cards.text: Then Paul goes further: "Indeed, I would rather die than let anyone nullify my boast." That's not a man politely turning down a favor, friend, that's a man DIVING in front of it.

cards.question: Paul says preaching the gospel gives him no reason to boast, because he is ___ to preach.

cards.text: Paul even says, "Woe to me if I do not preach the gospel!" And if his preaching isn't voluntary, he says he's still been entrusted with a responsibility.

cards.question: Then Paul asks, "What then is my reward?" What does he say it is?

answers.text: Offering the gospel free of charge
A home of his own someday

cards.text: Then Paul says something that sounds backward. He's free of obligation to anyone, but watch what he does with that freedom.

cards.question: True or false: Though Paul is free of obligation to anyone, he says he makes himself a slave to everyone, to win as many as possible.

cards.text: Paul lays it out group by group: "To the Jews I became like a Jew, to win the Jews." To those under the law, he became like one under the law, though he says he himself isn't under the law.

cards.question: To those without the law, Paul became like one without the law. But he says he's not outside the law of God. Whose law does he say he's under?

cards.text: Then Paul names one more group: "To the weak I became weak, to win the weak." He's meeting people right where they are, and me? I'm a cookie stamper, friend, I've stamped ONE shape my WHOLE life.

cards.question: Paul sums it up: he has become all things to all people so that by all possible means he might ___ some.
Paul says he does all this for the sake of the gospel. What does he hope for himself?

answers.text: To be known in every city
To rest from all his work

cards.text: Then Paul pulls out a new picture: "Do you not know that in a race all the runners run, but only one receives the prize?" Friend, I'm a stamper on a gold base, I don't run, I HOP, and I'm hopping in DEAD LAST.

cards.question: Only one runner gets the prize. True or false: Paul tells the Corinthians not to bother trying for it.

cards.text: Paul says everyone who competes in the games trains with strict discipline. STRICT discipline, friend, and I can't even keep my mustache out of the chocolate chips.

cards.question: Paul says the athletes train for a crown that is ___, but we do it for a crown that is ___.

cards.text: So Paul says, "I do not run aimlessly; I do not fight like I am beating the air." Not like me swinging my mustache at a fly for ten minutes, catching nothing but AIR.

cards.question: Instead of beating the air, Paul disciplines something and makes it his slave. What?
Paul says he disciplines his body and makes it his slave. After preaching to others, why does he do it?

answers.text: So he won't be disqualified himself
So the other apostles notice him
So the churches will honor him

cards.text: That's where we catch our breath for now, friend. Paul's not done talking to Corinth, not even close.
